This document serves as the starting point for the front end engineering design (FEED) of the CO 2 injection plant and contains information on the CO 2 stream properties from the OEE ethanol facility and injection site that are known at the time of writing. This document is organized into the following sections: • General facility design • Ambient conditions • Availability of utilities • CO 2 source characteristics • CO 2 production specifications • Process capacity and delivery requirements • Process monitoring requirements • Reliability and operability requirements General Facility Design This design utilizes a multistage centrifugal blower located near the fermenter that compresses the feed gas up to approximately 15 psig. The feed gas is further compressed by a five-stage reciprocating compressor to the required injection pressure. Between stages of the reciprocating compressor, the gas stream is cooled and condensed water is removed from the gas stream. After the 4th stage of compression, the gas stream flows through a packed tower that contacts the gas with triethylene glycol (TEG). At this pressure, the water content in CO 2 is relatively low, which reduces capital and operating costs of the dehydration unit, while the solubility of TEG in CO 2 is still low enough for economic operation. TEG losses would be too high in the CO 2 at the outlet of the 5th stage. The TEG absorbs water vapor present in the gas stream and dehydrates the gas to an extent that it is suitable for downstream equipment to be constructed from carbon steel. 2 The CO 2 produced in this process is not suitable for further use beyond injection and other than water, it retains most of the impurities present in the source CO 2 including any entrained O 2 . The major rotating equipment and associated equipment (such as separators and heat exchangers) will be located indoors. Dehydration equipment may be located indoors or outdoors, depending upon OEE’s preference, but all liquid containing vessels and outdoor lines will require heat tracing and insulation. The low pressure blower and associated knockouts will be located close to the fermenters so that condensed water can be reused in the ethanol plant. The compression trains will be located on the northwest corner of the facility, just north of the peaking plant. The facility will be located in a non-classified area. Ambient Conditions The OEE facility is located in Gibson City, IL which is approximately 30 miles northwest of Champaign, IL.
